facts.text: A project plan specifies what will be done, by whom and by when; a work package is a bounded chunk of that work; a deliverable is the concrete output handed over by a work package.
facts.quote: A project plan says what will be done, by whom and by when; a work package is one bounded chunk of that work; a deliverable is the concrete thing a work package hands over.

facts.text: The booklet requires every work package in the collision mitigation validation program to be tied to the safety evidence the work package will produce.
facts.quote: The booklet's distinctive rule is that every work package must be tied to the safety evidence it will produce.

facts.text: The central artifact of the collision mitigation validation plan should be an evidence plan, not merely a schedule: a ledger mapping each safety sub-claim to the required evidence, method, acceptance criterion, owner, work package, date and gate.
facts.quote: The central artifact of the plan should be an evidence plan, not merely a schedule: a ledger mapping each safety sub-claim to the evidence required, the method, the acceptance criterion, the owner, the work package, the date and the gate.

facts.text: Traceability in the collision mitigation validation evidence plan must run both ways; work or claims that cannot be connected deserve challenge because the work may be unnecessary or a claim may lack evidence.
facts.quote: Traceability must run both ways, and anything that cannot be connected in either direction deserves challenge: either it is unnecessary work or a claim lacks evidence [Chapter 12].

facts.text: The booklet's example deliverable cadence calls for a signed scope and context of use, an evidence tree and a schedule model by November 2026.
facts.quote: a signed scope and context of use, an evidence tree and a schedule model by November 2026

facts.text: The booklet's example deliverable cadence calls for a first end-to-end result and an unresolved-assumption report by January 2027.
facts.quote: a first end-to-end result and an unresolved-assumption report by January 2027

facts.text: The booklet's example deliverable cadence calls for a pilot evidence package by March 2027.
facts.quote: a pilot evidence package by March 2027 [Chapter 12].

facts.text: Rolling-wave planning details near-term work and outlines later work; the booklet describes rolling-wave planning as standard practice without outcome evidence.
facts.quote: Rolling-wave planning details near-term work and outlines later work; it is standard practice without outcome evidence.

facts.text: Discovery-driven planning makes early milestones learning milestones that establish whether something is possible, rather than reporting a feature as 80% coded.
facts.quote: Discovery-driven planning makes early milestones learning milestones: "we know whether X is possible" rather than "feature X is 80% coded" [Chapter 12].

facts.text: The collision mitigation validation plan will be reviewed by skeptical engineers, safety specialists and executives; a work package producing activity rather than evidence will not survive scrutiny of why the work package exists.
facts.quote: The plan will be reviewed by skeptical engineers, safety specialists and executives; a work package that produces activity rather than evidence will not survive their question "why does this exist?" [Chapter 12].
